karen-acme: Hey team — starting ~2023-09-14 18:12 UTC our streaming sessions to /v1/streams are dropping with partial output. Client sees ECONNRESET / EPIPE after a few chunks and then reconnect loops which blow up our token usage. Server-side we see lines like `writev failed: EPIPE` and `aborting stream: slow consumer (socket send buffer full)`. Request id header: req-0a1b2c3d. Using Node 16 EventSource polyfill behind a corporate proxy.

anna-support: Sorry about that — we can help. Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact x-request-id for a recent failing stream? Any chance you can reproduce with curl so we can try from our side? Also are you seeing this only through your corporate proxy or from direct connections too? :thinking_face:

karen-acme: Repro steps below — this reproduces locally by throttling the reader so the server has to buffer. We see partial chunks then connection reset after ~25s.

```
# server-side: POST to /v1/streams with a streaming response
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' \\
  | pv -qL 30  # slow consumer: limit read to 30 bytes/sec
```

Client logs show:
- fetch error: request aborted (ECONNRESET)
- EventSource: got partial event, then connection closed

Server logs (excerpt):
- [2023-09-14T18:12:23Z] req-0a1b2c3d writev failed: EAGAIN
- [2023-09-14T18:12:23Z] req-0a1b2c3d writev failed: EPIPE
- [2023-09-14T18:12:23Z] req-0a1b2c3d aborting stream: slow_consumer (sendbuf_full)

mike-sre: Thanks, that matches a slow-consumer backpressure path we've seen. Two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm if you hit this via our hosted API or through a dedicated/private deployment? (proxy behavior differs)
2) Please share the gateway + runtime trace ids around that timestamp (x-request-id header on client and any trace IDs in the server logs).

A bit of context: when the kernel SO_SNDBUF fills and subsequent send/writev returns EAGAIN repeatedly, our runtime tries limited retries. If the client still isn't pulling, the runtime switches to an abort path to avoid unbounded memory growth and will close the socket which shows up as EPIPE/ECONNRESET to the client. That produces partial output and triggers client reconnects which can spiral.

liam-eng: A few mitigation suggestions while we investigate:
- Try to speed up client reads (increase max socket buffer on client OS or reduce client-side throttling).
- Use HTTP/2 or direct connection (bypassing proxies that may buffer bigger chunks). Some proxies buffer whole responses and amplify backpressure.
- On server side we can reduce chunk sizes and lower aggressive writev coalescing. As a temporary client-side workaround, have the client send a small keepalive read (or read loop) more frequently so the kernel drains the socket.

Quick repro curl that helped us locally (simulate slow consumer with pv):
```
# from a machine outside of your corp-proxy
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams -d '{"prompt":"stream test"}' | pv -qL 50
```

liam-eng: Technically the runtime writes frames with writev up to a certain threshold. If the pipe is blocked, writev returns EAGAIN; after N retries we log and abort to keep the worker sane. We can tune N and the retry backoff, but that risks memory pressure. I'll instrument more logging for write queue length and the exact errno sequence.

sophia-cs: For customers hitting this in production we recommend two options:
- Short-term: Reduce client-side read throttling and avoid intermediaries that buffer (eg corp proxies). Also reduce chunking frequency and enable small keepalives.
- Medium-term: Move heavy streaming to Dedicated capacity (avoids shared proxy buffers and gives more predictable handling) or bump the connection-level window if using HTTP/2.

anna-support: I'll open an internal ticket to escalate to eng-runtime. Karen, can you DM me the account id, last 4 of the API key, and attach a pcap or tcpdump around 2023-09-14T18:12:20-18:12:30Z? We want the client-side capture (shows delayed ACKs/proxy buffering) and the gateway logs.

karen-acme: Sent the pcap and logs to support@redwood with subject "streaming partial + EPIPE req-0a1b2c3d". We're still seeing billing increments from reconnect loops so would appreciate a fast turnaround. :pray:

deploy-bot: Created ticket ENG-2045: "sse slow-consumer write aborts -> partial outputs + reconnect billing" assigned to liam-eng.

liam-eng: I'll take ENG-2045. Next steps: reproduce in a controlled env with a slow reader, collect writev errno sequences, add faster log points in the send loop, and propose a safe retry/backoff change. ETA EOD PST for initial findings.

anna-support: Thanks everyone — we'll update this thread once eng posts a fix or mitigation. If you get a full repro that doesn't use the corp proxy, please paste it here; proxies are often the root cause. :thumbsup:

karen-acme: Thanks, appreciate the quick response. We'll try the curl + pv test from outside the corp network and report results in the thread.
